title: Two ipamd metrics are renamed (awscni_err_no_avail_addrs, awscni_eni_util)

detection.reason: alert rules and dashboards that query the metrics are outside the cluster objects collected

remediation: Update alerts and dashboards: awscni_err_no_avail_addrs → awscni_no_available_ip_addresses and awscni_eni_util → awscni_assigned_ip_per_eni (73ccf51f). Queries on the old names silently return no data after the upgrade — an IP-exhaustion alert keyed on the old name stops firing.
verifyCommand: kubectl get prometheusrules -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | select(tostring | test("awscni_err_no_avail_addrs|awscni_eni_util")) | "\(.metadata.namespace)/\(.metadata.name)"'  # each PrometheusRule printed still queries a metric name that no longer exists after v1.15.1

title: v1.15.4–v1.16.1 write cniVersion 1.0.0 into 10-aws.conflist (reverted in v1.16.2)

detection.reason: which plugins are chained after aws-cni lives in the node's /etc/cni/net.d conflist

remediation: Only a cluster that lands on v1.15.4–v1.16.1 runs with cniVersion 1.0.0 (v1.16.2 reverts to 0.4.0). A chained or meta plugin (Cilium chaining, Multus, Calico policy-only, istio-cni) must support CNI spec 1.0.0 there — skip those patches rather than stopping on them.
verifyCommand: kubectl get ds -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select([.spec.template.spec.containers[].image] | any(test("cilium|multus|calico|istio-cni|install-cni|linkerd"))) | "\(.metadata.namespace)/\(.metadata.name)"'  # each DaemonSet printed chains onto the VPC CNI and must accept cniVersion 1.0.0 if the cluster stops on v1.15.4-v1.16.1

title: The bandwidth plugin is not supported together with VPC CNI network policy

detection.reason: ENABLE_BANDWIDTH_PLUGIN's VALUE is not collected; --enable-network-policy is an arg of the aws-eks-nodeagent container

quote: Bandwidth plugin with NP is currently unsupported
remediation: Do not run ENABLE_BANDWIDTH_PLUGIN=true together with the network policy agent enforcing (--enable-network-policy=true): both program the pod's tc (traffic control) hooks and policy enforcement fails (aws/aws-network-policy-agent#68). Turn one of them off before enabling the other.
verifyCommand: kubectl -n kube-system get ds aws-node -o json | jq -r '[.spec.template.spec.containers[] | (.env[]? | select(.name == "ENABLE_BANDWIDTH_PLUGIN") | "\(.name)=\(.value)"), (.args[]? | select(test("^--enable-network-policy")))] | join(" ")'  # ENABLE_BANDWIDTH_PLUGIN=true together with --enable-network-policy=true is the unsupported combination

title: aws-node needs get/list/watch on cninodes.vpcresources.k8s.aws from v1.15 — apply the release ClusterRole
quote: Add watch permission for CNINode resource
remediation: From v1.15 ipamd reads CNINode objects (the VPC Resource Controller's per-node feature record) and its informer needs list/watch on cninodes.vpcresources.k8s.aws. Upgrade with the release manifest / chart / EKS add-on so the aws-node ClusterRole gains the rule — an image-only bump leaves the old ClusterRole and the watch is forbidden.
verifyCommand: kubectl get clusterrole aws-node -o json | jq -r '[.rules[] | select((.apiGroups // []) | index("vpcresources.k8s.aws")) | .verbs[]] | unique | join(",")'  # empty, or no list/watch printed = the aws-node ClusterRole predates v1.15 and cannot watch CNINode
coversNotes: Feature - Add support for VPC Resource Controller's CNINode (reintroduce #2442)
